successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: the Moabite plateau; the Cliopatria Achaemenid shape of -404 covers it

ledger.x: c. 1250 BCE: Moab arises east of the Dead Sea. Infobox 'Established: c. 13th century BCE'; 'The statue lists Mu'ab among a series of nations conquered during a campaign' (Ramesses II's Luxor statue, 13th century). A century is not a year; mid-century is a convention. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: region widened to…

c. 1000 BC (bridged): David makes Moab tributary. 'In the Books of Samuel account, Moab is said to have been conquered by David (traditional floruit c. 1000-970 BC)' and 'retained in the territories of his son Solomon (d. c. 931 BC)'; the Moab page cites 2 Samuel 8:2 and 1 Chronicles 18:2 for the Moabites…

c. 931 BC (bridged): Moab is lost to Israel after Solomon. The Mesha page has Moab 'retained in the territories of his son Solomon (d. c. 931 BC)' and 'lost subsequent to King Solomon's reign'; -930 mirrors the vassal_end moab of kingdom-of-israel. The Moab page differs: it says Moab 'continued in vassalage…

c. 880 BC (bridged): Omri puts Moab under Israel again. The Omri page gives the reign as 885-874 BC and says the Mesha Stele 'makes reference to the oppression of Moab by "Omri King of Israel"' and that Omri 'expanded his holdings to include northern Moab east of…

c. 850 BC: Mesha throws off Israel. 'The stele records Mesha's liberation of Moab from under the suzerainty of Israel in c. 850 BC'; the Moab page dates the rebellion to the death of Ahab 'about 853 BCE' (Thiele) and Mesha to c. 870-840 BCE. The Mesha Stele itself is 'dated around 840 BCE'. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19…

c. 850 BC: Mesha takes Medeba and the towns north of Wadi el-Wale. The Moab page: Mesha 'conquered the Israelite territory north of Wadi el-Wale with the cities of Medeba, Ataroth and Nebo'; the stele page has Ataroth ('I assaulted the wall and captured it'), Nebo ('I took it') and Horonaim ('I took it'); the stele…
734 BC: Moab pays tribute to Assyria.

c. 609 BCE (bridged): Assyria's overlordship ends. No page opened dates when Moab stopped paying Assyria; the year mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire dossier's close of the 734 tributaries, and the Nebuchadnezzar page shows Moab under Babylonian control by 594. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: Moab page re-read: it does not…

c. 609 BCE (bridged): Moab passes to Babylon. The Nebuchadnezzar page has 'in Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah (594 BC), the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre met in Jerusalem' to discuss throwing off Babylonian control, and the Moab page has Moab 'later aided Nebuchadnezzar in his expedition against…
c. 400 BCE (bridged): the Persian overlordship closes with the kingdom's collapse; the page names no conqueror. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: added to close the vassalage opened in -539.].

c. 400 BCE: the kingdom of Moab collapses. Infobox 'Collapsed: c. 400 BCE'; the page names no conqueror and says only that after Pompey's conquest of the Levant in 63 BCE Moab lost its distinct identity.

wars.name: Mesha's revolt against Israel
wars.outcome: Mesha's stele claims a decisive victory and the recovery of Medeba, Nebo, Jahaz and the towns north of the Arnon; 2 Kings 3:27 says Israel's army 'withdrew from him and returned to their own land' after the siege of the Moabite capital.

wars.name: Ashdod revolt and the regional coalition against Sargon II
wars.outcome: 'In 711 BCE, Moab entered into a regional coalition with Edom and Judah in rebellion against the Assyrian King'; Moab 'avoided the direct retribution Ashdod suffered'.

wars.name: Moab's rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar II
wars.outcome: 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'; outcome not on the page.

certainty.note: The Arnon northern boundary is 'likely fluid' (Moab page); Heshbon is a border town between Moab and Ammon of ambiguous status.
